info.title: Kast callable reference
info.description: Public compiler-grounded Kast callables invoked through the Kast CLI.

post.description:
Search, filter, and expand exact Kotlin symbols. Use SEARCH for names, ALL for enumeration, or REFS for returned exact-symbol tokens. Omitted controls use the defaults documented in the parameter contract. Kast owns candidate refinement and bounded work; incomplete coverage stays explicit.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Find bounded Kotlin declaration candidates in the current workspace. Use when an exact selector is not already available. Returned candidate selectors are proof-carrying identities and must be preserved verbatim.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Refine a candidate into exact compiler-grounded symbol identity or inspect an existing exact selector. Prefer the returned exact selector over reconstructing symbol identity from source text.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Read bounded source and structural context around a candidate, exact symbol, or source selector. Prefer this over unrestricted filesystem reads when the required Kotlin context is representable through Kast.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Read one bounded compiler-grounded semantic relation from an exact selector. Use kast.query first when exact identity is not established.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Perform bounded transitive semantic traversal from an exact selector. Required topology is acquired automatically for the current generation; the caller does not prepare it separately.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Check bounded compiler diagnostics beneath a workspace-relative file or directory path. Use `.` for the workspace root. Prefer this when compiler-grounded diagnostic identity matters.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Derive a bounded change plan from an exact target without writing source. Preserve the returned plan identity for apply or recovery.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Apply one previously derived Kast change plan and return its verified receipt. Requires explicit approval and the exact returned plan identity.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

Recover one applied Kast change plan to a known workspace state. Requires explicit approval and the exact returned plan identity.

This callable is not an HTTP endpoint. Invoke it with the Kast CLI command shown in the example.

QUERY_RUNRequest.description: Agent-facing query syntax. Defaults are fixed by this contract, not by the environment. This schema does not confer compiler authority.

QueryText.description: Declaration name to match. Blank text is rejected; use ALL for enumeration. At most 256 UTF-16 code units at canonical admission.

ExactRef.description: Copy items[].ref.token from an exact-symbol result verbatim. This prefix check is syntax only; Kast still validates workspace, read authority and compiler identity.

DirectoryPath.description: Canonical path relative to the workspace root. A single dot means the root. Absolute paths, backslashes, empty segments, embedded dot segments and parent traversal are rejected; spelling is preserved.

PackageName.description: Semantic Kotlin package name; not a path. Uses the currently supported ASCII package-name grammar.

Match.description: Omitted means exact declaration-name matching. Exact does not select one overload. Fuzzy matching requires explicit opt-in.

DeclarationKind.description: Supported discovery family. Class includes the existing class-like family; constructors are not discoverable through this source.

SourceSet.description: Exact Gradle source-set name from the imported model, including custom and multiplatform names. Not a production/test category or filesystem glob.

Containment.description: Omitted searches recursively, including this directory or package and all nested directories or subpackages. DIRECT selects only this directory or package.

Relation.description: One compiler-confirmed semantic hop. Callers returns calling declarations; callees returns called declarations.

Field.description: Optional result projection. Existing ref and kind fields are always retained.

Kinds.description: Omitted includes every supported discovery family. Empty and duplicate lists are rejected.

SourceSets.description: Omitted selects names main and test. Explicit names intersect with directory and package restrictions; names with no matching roots contribute no declarations.

Selection.description: Omitted returns name and location. Empty requests ref and kind only; it does not restore defaults.

Steps.description: Ordered left-to-right transformations. Omitted means no steps. Never reorder filters around expansion.

RefsList.description: Non-empty returned exact-symbol tokens. No candidate promotion, guessing or alias lookup.

VisibilityList.description: Non-empty set of accepted visibilities; unproved predicates remain incomplete evidence, never a negative match.

Scope.description: Exactly one directory or package target. Source-set restrictions intersect with the target. Containment applies to either target. Scope does not restrict later expansion destinations.

type.description: Selects the grammar and meaning of value.

Search.description: Find matching declarations and establish exact compiler identities. Multiple overloads remain separate symbols.

All.description: Explicit bounded enumeration. Budget exhaustion remains partial coverage; ALL never implies unbounded work.

Refs.description: Start from exact-symbol references previously returned by Kast.

Source.description: Every source yields exact symbols or explicit incomplete/rejected evidence. Candidates are internal to Kast.

Filter.description: Filter the current symbol stream by compiler-established visibility.

Expand.description: Expand the current symbols by exactly one semantic hop, retaining relation evidence.

Distinct.description: Deduplicate exact symbols using the existing engine operation, preserving contributing relation evidence.

Step.description: Closed symbol-to-symbol transformations. INSPECT is intentionally not public.

ScopeValue.description: DIRECTORY: canonical workspace-relative path, with . for the root. PACKAGE: dotted Kotlin package name. The typed parser validates the grammar selected by type.
